body.claim: The software for the Apollo Guidance Computer was woven into core rope memory by female workers in factories.
body.why: In core rope memory, sense wires encode data by either going through a core or bypassing it. In the Apollo Guidance Computer, each core had 192 sense wires passing through it, which could store twelve 16-bit words per core. Some programmers nicknamed the finished product LOL memory, for Little Old Lady memory.

probes.question: In core rope memory, how are bits of data encoded?
options: A sense wire goes through a core or bypasses it
A hole is punched in a card
A switch is flipped on a chip
A spot on a disk is magnetized
